$comment: RFU document acquisition log, recorded under the standing acquisition rule.
THE AUTHORITY IS ALWAYS THE RFU. canonical_source_url is the provenance a
published fact cites, regardless of where the bytes were actually obtained.
A mirror is only ever an ACQUISITION COPY -- a way to get the file -- and
englandrugby.com returns HTTP 403 to every automated request, including
robots.txt, at the CloudFront layer. That control was NOT circumvented: no
proxy rotation, no client spoofing, no challenge bypass, no session reuse.
The block is recorded as a fact about acquisition, not worked around.
OUTCOME: no candidate mirror establishes equivalence with the CURRENT
season's official document. Every candidate is therefore
NEEDS_HUMAN_SOURCE_VERIFICATION and no fact may be extracted from any of
them. A one-time human download is requested (see ingestion_request).

UPDATE 2026-09-07: the developer supplied the official Regulation 15 appendix text directly, after automated retrieval was refused. Phase 4B extraction for Union age grades is unblocked. See ingestion_request.fulfilment.

candidates.reasoning: The TEXT appears to be the RFU's, but the FILE is not. A Word document authored by a named individual is a re-creation, not an exact copy: it could have been retyped, reflowed, abridged or edited, and nothing in it says which season it represents. The 2024 upload date is misleading -- the file itself was made in 2023. This is precisely the failure mode the acquisition rule exists to catch, and the recency of the upload is exactly what would have made it tempting.

conflict_detected.why_it_matters: Phase 4A recorded Union girls age grades as RESEARCH_REQUIRED on the grounds that we had not established whether girls' Rules of Play differ. One constituent body says they demonstrably do and names the appendix; the other does not list it. Both are reputable, neither is authority, and neither states a season -- so the difference may be a genuine regulatory change that one body has not reflected, or simply a stale page.
conflict_detected.resolution: UNRESOLVED. Not resolved by preferring the newer-looking or more detailed page. Resolving it requires the RFU's own current Regulation 15 index, which is behind the 403. Girls age grades therefore REMAIN RESEARCH_REQUIRED, and no girls identity is created on the strength of a county page.
conflict_detected.effect_on_publication: Blocking for all Union girls identities.

The rule applied is identical in every case: canonical provenance is the governing body's own URL, equivalence is verified before anything is extracted, and a document that cannot be shown to be current is banked rather than used.

acquisitions.reasoning: This is the inverse of the usual failure mode. Provenance is not the problem -- it is as strong as the Full Rules and was proved by direct comparison against the governing body's own host. What fails is currency. Two 2026 editions exist by the same author; the RFL links only the later, longer one. Whether this is a superseded draft or a condensed handout cannot be decided from the files themselves, because both embed subset fonts that defeat text extraction, and under either reading it is not what the RFL currently presents. Recorded rather than discarded because the URL is still live but orphaned, and would otherwise be rediscovered and mistaken for current. If the two documents' rule values were ever to disagree, the Full Rules governs.

verification.document_title: VERIFIED from the document's own text - 'RFU REGULATION 15 - AGE GRADE RUGBY'
verification.appendix_number: VERIFIED - 'Appendix 10', stated on the cover and repeated in the running head
verification.season_or_version: VERIFIED - 'Effective from 1 August 2017', stated in the document
verification.publication_metadata: STRONG - Adobe InDesign CS6 (Macintosh) / Adobe PDF Library 10.0.1, created 2017-07-07 15:59. The independently retrieved RFURegulation15-2017.18.pdf (ACQ-RFU-REG15-2017-WHITEROSE) carries the same toolchain and a creation date in the same week. Neither file's provenance depends on the other, so the match is real mutual corroboration that both are genuine RFU-produced 2017 artefacts.

acquisitions.reasoning: Answers a structural question decisively and a factual one not at all. Appendix 10 for U13 girls demonstrably existed in 2017, so Gloucestershire RFU's listing of it is not an invention and the disagreement with Nottinghamshire, Lincolnshire & Derbyshire RFU is no longer a straight choice between a correct page and a wrong one. What it cannot show is whether Appendix 10 survives into 2025/26 -- a document from nine seasons ago is evidence about 2017 and nothing else.
acquisitions.publication_prohibition: Its rule values must NOT be published as current rules, and a '(taken from a 2017 copy)' disclaimer does not make them publishable. The developer raised exactly this option and the answer is no, for a reason specific to this product: a parent who opens Ovalball to find their U13 daughter's ball size or half length acts on the number, not the footnote, and age-grade Rules of Play have changed materially since 2017 -- the RFU's own current set is dated 'Effective from Friday 1st August 2025'. A wrong safety-relevant value carrying a date caveat is more dangerous than no value, because the caveat transfers the risk to the reader while the number still reads as authoritative. The correct use is the one taken here: bank it as historical evidence that resolves the structural question, and leave the U12-U14 girls facts unpublished until the current appendix index is confirmed.

It settled two questions that months of county-page corroboration could not: 15.2(2)(a) enumerates the Rules of Play as 'Appendix 1 to 9' (closing the Appendix 10 dispute), and 15.6 defines the girls game as four dual age bands (closing the girls age-grade question and forcing a correction to Ovalball's own canonical team types). carried_forward.authorisation_text: use them even though they 25/26 that's absolutely fine
carried_forward.recorded_as: regulatory_sources.carries_forward = true on all nine, each with a written carries_forward_note
carried_forward.justification: Master Regulation 15 (2026/27) section 15.2(2)(a) requires play 'in accordance with the Rules of Play set out Appendix 1 to 9 of this Regulation', pointing at the appendices without dating them. These nine pages are what the RFU publishes under that master today, so a club following the RFU's own website is following exactly these documents.
carried_forward.residual_risk: If the RFU reissues the appendices mid-season, the carries_forward flag is what makes that detectable: a newer source with a 2026/27 effective date trips the season-compatibility guard rather than silently coexisting.

open_question.what: Appendices 1-8 never mention gender. Master 15.6 defines the girls game as dual age bands (U12/U11, U14/U13, U16/U15, U18/U17). Below U15 it is not stated which appendix governs a girls band -- e.g. does the U14/U13 band play Appendix 8 (U14) or Appendix 7 (U13)?
open_question.why_it_matters: The two readings give different ball sizes, pitch sizes, scrum sizes and half lengths for the same child.
open_question.resolved_for: U15-U18 only, where Appendix 9 states its own gender scope explicitly.
